brief.topic: The Space That Survives a Changing Outline

s01: A patch of space leans to one side.
Its outline changes, but has any area disappeared?
Keep its base and its height fixed.
Now cut this small triangle from the right.
Slide the same piece across to the left.
Nothing was stretched, added, or thrown away.
The leaning shape has become a rectangle.
So its area is base times height.
The height is the straight distance between these parallel edges.
It is not the sloping side.
Let the shape lean the other way.
Each horizontal slice still has the same length.
The layers slide, but the space they make stays unchanged.
Sometimes a new outline is simply the same amount of room, rearranged.

scenes.narration:
A patch of space leans to one side. Its outline changes, but has any area disappeared?

Keep its base and its height fixed. Now cut this small triangle from the right. Slide the same piece across to the left.

It fits the gap exactly. Nothing was stretched, added, or thrown away. The leaning shape has become a rectangle.

So its area is base times height. The height is the straight distance between these parallel edges. It is not the sloping side.

Let the shape lean the other way. Each horizontal slice still has the same length. The layers slide, but the space they make stays unchanged. Sometimes a new outline is simply the same amount of room, rearranged.
